text:
anya: heads up — prod prefix hit-rate collapsed on a subset of eu runtime pods after we flipped prefetch_affinity_window from 3s -> 0.5s. seeing p50 generation latency jump ~80ms -> ~220ms for short-chat traffic. anyone looking? :eyes:

matt: which pods/hostnames? is it across all zones?

anya: narrow to prod-eu-rtus pool, node label r4g-highmem, 5/18 pods showing hit-rate < 20%. others still ~80%. not global. started ~06:12 UTC after the deploy/flag flip.

raj: that flag was toggled in the runtime prefetch PR that also changed the batching heuristic for short sequences. cc @sophia in case the model/kernel routing is relevant. PR link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/rtus/merge/4223

sophia: can you paste the prometheus queries? want host-level kv metrics and evictions.

anya: prom queries I ran:
```
avg by(pod) (rate(kv_cache_prefix_hitrate_total[5m]))
rate(kv_cache_prefix_evictions_total[5m])
sum by(pod) (rate(request_latency_seconds_count{route="generate"}[5m]))
```
outputs: pod eu-rtus-7 dropped from 0.82 -> 0.11 over 10m, evictions spiked from ~2/min -> ~480/min on that pod.

infra-bot: alert: KV_PREFIX_HITRATE_DROP on prod-eu-rtus (eu-rtus-7). trigger at 2026-03-18T06:14:02Z. linked runbook: /runbooks/kv-hitrate-falls.md :rotating_light:

matt: grabbing pprof from the affected pod now. will look for hotspots and kernel fallbacks.

matt: pprof flamegraph (top frames):
- runtime::evict_prefixes (heavy)
- kernel::select_opt_kernel (increasing fallback to scalar_int8_slow)
- batching::adjust_window (tight loop)
Noting a lot of time spent in eviction paths and in kernel fallback overhead.

raj: that matches theory: tighter prefetch window increases churn in prefix caching; combined with "aggressive_small_batch" heuristic we shipped, small seqs are frequently primed then evicted. kernel selector then picks slower fallback for many requests because warm-up/primed paths aren't stable.

anya: good catch. do we have a config diff from last night's deploy?

sophia: config diff: prefetch_affinity_window: 3.0 -> 0.5
batching_heuristics.aggressive_small_batch.enabled: false -> true
kernel_routing.thresholds.int8_warmup: 0.95 -> 0.98
(to be clear: we tightened warmup threshold and enabled aggressive batching)

matt: here's a quick one-liner to roll the flag back for the deployment (k8s patch):
```bash
kubectl -n prod patch deploy rtus --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/0/value","value":"3.0"}]'
```
(verify the env index before applying)

anya: initiating rollback of prefetch_affinity_window to 3.0 now. will keep aggressive batching toggled until we validate.

infra-bot: deploy started: rolling update for deployment/rtus in namespace prod at 2026-03-18T06:22:10Z.

matt: watching metrics — evictions on eu-rtus-7 dropping within 2 mins of rollback. prefix hit-rate climbing: 0.11 -> 0.42 -> 0.75 over 8 minutes. p50 latency falling back toward baseline.

anya: confirmed recovery on the impacted pods. looks like the prefetch window change was the root trigger, exacerbated by the batching heuristic and stricter kernel warmup threshold.

raj: action items: 1) revert prefetch change in prod (done), 2) create a canary test for prefetch_affinity_window that monitors kv evictions and kernel fallback rate before rolling wide, 3) add a guard that prevents enabling aggressive_small_batch simultaneously with prefetch window < 1s, 4) instrument kernel selector to emit fallback-rate metric per-pod.

sophia: I'll file the postmortem and assign owners (pf:anya, perf: matt, infra: raj). will include graphs, pprof, config diff, and suggested followups.

anya: thanks all. recommend we add a quick telemetry alert that correlates kv_prefix_evictions with kernel_fallback_rate so rollbacks are faster next time. :thumbsup:

matt: agree. also add a low-risk experiment to try prefetch_affinity_window=1.5s with aggressive batching on trimmed canary to see behavior.

raj: noted — will draft a safe-enablement checklist for the next change.

anya: closing thread as recovered, will follow up in the postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:
